title: Israeli strike kills 2 senior Hamas officials
summary: The second strike left four people dead, including two children. Witnesses say they were given no prior warning and the explosion happened in the middle of the night, while everyone was sleeping.

image.caption: Mourners carry the bodies of Muhammad Abu al-Ouf, a Hamas internal security officer, and his family, during their funeral in Gaza City. They were killed in an Israeli strike. (Jehad Alshrafi/The Associated Press)

blocks.text: World·New
The second strike left four people dead, including two children. Witnesses say they were given no prior warning and the explosion happened in the middle of the night, while everyone was sleeping.
Israel says it was targeting Hamas officials in charge of security in northern Gaza

It was a chaotic scene in the Al Shati refugee camp in Gaza City after an Israeli strike hit an apartment building, leaving four dead and multiple injuries. It shattered the facade and left furniture and toys strewn on the ground.
Witnesses say multiple people were sheltering nearby and the strike came with no prior notice.

The Israel Defence Forces (IDF) said they were targeting a senior Hamas security official who was sheltering in the building with his wife and two children. Mohammad Abuelouf was a Hamas colonel who headed the militant’s internal security service in northern Gaza.
It was the second senior Hamas security official killed in the last 24 hours. Yesterday afternoon, IDF targeted Naim Abu Nahal in a displacement camp in Gaza City — he was also the head of security.
A Palestinian man inspects an apartment destroyed in an Israeli strike in Gaza City. (Jehad Alshrafi/The Associated Press)

IDF strikes have continued throughout the ceasefire as Israel insists it will go after Hamas officials until they lay down their arms. Peace talks have not moved beyond the first phase announced last October and both sides blame the other for the lack of progress.
Mahmoud Bakr, 33, was sheltering near the site of the strike when the explosion happened. He says there’s no safety in Gaza.
"This is what you call a ceasefire?" he told CBC freelance videographer Mohamed El Saife. "If, while we’re sleeping bombs fall on us, then where is the ceasefire?"

The Israeli military confirmed it had killed Abuelouf, whom it described as a ​significant figure who "served as a key source of expertise in efforts to restrict the IDF’s ⁠counterterrorism operations in the Gaza Strip."

Despite a year-old ceasefire, Israel has continued to carry out attacks that it ​says target Hamas but have also killed many civilians. The broader ceasefire plan, backed by U.S. President Donald Trump, ​has not halted the violence or secured Hamas's disarmament.
Palestinian children look at an apartment destroyed in an Israeli strike in Gaza City. (Jehad Alshrafi/The Associated Press)

Medics said Wednesday's airstrike had ripped through Abuelouf's apartment in the Beach refugee camp in western Gaza City, near the coast. Later in the morning, another Israeli airstrike hit Gaza City's northern Karama neighbourhood, killing one person, medics said.

The Israeli military said Abuelouf had helped, during the war and more recently, to advance attacks ​against Israeli forces and civilians and had worked to restore the capabilities of Hamas in violation of the 2025 ceasefire deal.

In a statement posted to Telegram, Hamas called the attack a "massacre." They said the latest targeting of Abuelouf "constitutes a flagrant violation of international and humanitarian laws, and reflects its determination to press ahead with its plans of genocide."
On Tuesday, after the military killed Naeem Abu Nahel, Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu said there was no escape for Hamas from his country's "long reach."
Israel controls two-thirds of Gaza
At least 1,600 Palestinians and five Israeli soldiers have been killed since the ceasefire was struck ​in October 2025, according to respective Palestinian and Israeli tallies.
Israeli troops now control around ​two-thirds of Gaza, ⁠up from more than half at the time of the ceasefire, with Hamas controlling a sliver of territory along Gaza's coast.

Gaza’s Board of Peace delivered an update on its progress to the United Nations Security Council earlier this month, warning diplomats of a collapse of the fragile agreement if steps are not taken for full implementation.
The BoP report calls on both Israel and Hamas to uphold the commitments made last year under the agreement and urges the UN’s most powerful body to lend its support to the execution of its plan.
Palestinians inspect the wreckage of a car hit by an Israeli strike in Gaza City. (Jehad Alshrafi/The Associated Press)

"The distance between what has been agreed and what is happening on the ground nonetheless remains the principal risk to the process," says the report, a copy of which was obtained by The Associated Press.

It is the latest admonishment from the board in recent weeks, as deadly Israeli strikes and the continued blocking of humanitarian aid to Gaza have caused widespread hardship to the civilian population, which the board says is set to face "another winter in tents and rubble."

Israel says it has allowed 91,000 tents into Gaza over the past three months, a quantity far short of the number the UN says is needed, since much of the territory’s population of almost two million rely on them for shelter and they do not last long. It says it has 100,000 more tents waiting to be allowed into Gaza.

"Restrictions imposed by Israel on the entry of supplies and equipment, compounded by funding shortfalls, continued to impede preparedness and response efforts," the report said, calling for immediate "scaled-up entry of shelter and winterization materials" and approvals for pumps, generators and heavy machinery.
ABOUT THE AUTHOR
